newsitem.title: INDIA: Active debt market can boost India's growth rate.
newsitem.headline: Active debt market can boost India's growth rate.

text.p: India could boost its economic growth rate to over seven percent in the next few years by taking steps to activate the debt market and create transparent regulatory structures, a senior economist said on Saturday.

"A growth rate of seven to eight percent is sustainable provided measures are taken to activate the debt market, create transparency in regulatory structures and provide fiscal support through tax benefits," said Rakesh Mohan, director general of India's National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER).
Mohan was addressing a conference on finance and investment in the Indian capital.
India's Planning Commission, the country's apex plan panel, has forecast an annual growth rate of 7.0 percent during the period of the ninth five-year-plan, scheduled to start on April 1, 1997.
Mohan said India needed to take steps to activate the capital market by establishing a single regulatory authority and fixing a single rate of taxation for all debt instruments.
The capital market currently contributes around 300 billion rupees for infrastructure development, he said.
"It is expected to go up to 450 billion rupees by 2001," Mohan said.
Investment in infrastructure should be made lucrative to attract more private sector participation, he said.
"Private sector investment in infrastructure is currently around 120 billion which is expected to go up to around 380 billion by 2001," Mohan added.
